_why: THE HAND-MADE FEED CURATION, CAPTURED SO THE BUILD REPRODUCES IT (#1309).
Owner's ruling, 2026-08-27: "I like the handmade edits. Codify them." The
published feed ordering and hero placement on site_a were made by hand, directly
on the per-site posts.json, across six passes between 2025-07-29 and 2025-08-18.
The assembler knows nothing about them, so every re-assembly threw them away.
WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT
It is a record of VALUES. It is not a record of REASONING.
Nobody wrote down why post X was dated before post Y, and this file cannot
recover it. It can only say what was chosen. That has a consequence worth
stating plainly: if the underlying posts change, a curated ordering can stop
making sense and the document will go on applying it anyway. A curated hero
still sits first even if it is no longer the picture worth leading with.
So each entry carries `pipeline_members`, a digest of the membership the
curation was authored against. `apply_post_curation` re-derives it and REPORTS
every post whose membership has moved since. That does not tell you whether the
curation is still good, which nothing can; it tells you where to look.
HOW THE VALUES WERE RECOVERED. The share keeps eight `posts.json.pre-*.bak`
files beside the live one. Walked in mtime order they give six curation passes:
pre-hero      -> pre-hero2    created_at 841, asset_ids 385, updated_at 288
pre-hero2     -> pre-hero2b   asset_ids 79
pre-hero2b    -> pre-hero2c   updated_at 12, created_at 12
pre-feedcurate  -> pre-feedcurate2  created_at 823
pre-feedcurate2 -> pre-1217         created_at 794
⛔ ONE STEP IN THAT SEQUENCE IS NOT A CURATION PASS AND IS SKIPPED.
pre-hero2c -> pre-feedcurate drops the row count from 859 to 847 while the id
count stays at 847: it is the #1293 id-collision dedupe, not an edit. Walked as
a curation pass it appears to change 6 titles, 8 memberships, 2 descriptions, 2
tag lists and 4 more values. It changes none of them. Those are simply the
values of whichever of two colliding rows survived, and the titles it would
have pinned are the generated ones #1306 removed:
a Props roundup titled with an em dash and '10 drops', replaced by the same
title with '8 drops' after the ten-member row lost to the eight-member one
Both sides of that are generator output. Codifying it would re-pin a machine
title, em dash and all, onto an id that no longer collides.
Nothing changed after `pre-1217`: the two later backups and the live file only
ADD posts. So a post edited by several passes needs no conflict rule here, and
there is none. The chain says WHICH (post, field) pairs a human touched; the
live file says what the last pass left there, and that is the value recorded.
⛔ NO TITLE IS CURATED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE REASON THE CHAIN IS USED RATHER
THAN A PLAIN DIFF. The published posts.json disagrees with the pipeline on 780
titles. Not one of them is a hand edit: 774 are #1306, which deliberately
rewrote the seeded titles to drop the em dashes and the generated counts, and
the remaining 6 are the dedupe above. Diffing published against pipeline and
codifying the result would have reverted #1306 on 774 posts, and it would have
looked like it worked.
The same test excludes the 68 ids that #1293 moved onto the membership-derived
key: those are read through `post-id-migration.studio-a.json`, so this document
is keyed on today's ids throughout.
⛔ FIVE CURATED MEMBERSHIPS ARE EXCLUDED, FOR THE SAME REASON THE TITLES ARE.
383 of the 388 curated `asset_ids` hold the same assets in a different order:
that is the hero placement, and it is what this document is for. Five hold a
DIFFERENT SET, and all five are `team_roundup` or `project_sprint`, whose ids
derive from membership under ADR 0098. Applying them would make those ids stop
deriving from the posts they name.
They are not edits either. The five go 10 members to 8, 8 to 6, 8 to 7, 9 to 6
and 10 to 5, which are the same five posts whose titles moved in the dedupe
step above. They are the losing rows of the #1293 collision, which the published
feed kept under the winner's id. Their `created_at` and `updated_at` curation is
kept; only the membership is left to the assembler.
⚠️ THIS PASS OVERWRITES, unlike `apply_manifest_reconcile`, which can only add.
It has to: reproducing a chosen date means replacing a derived one. Its safety
property is narrower and stated in its docstring: it writes only the fields
NAMED in an entry, only onto a post that already exists, and it never creates,
deletes or reorders posts.
